statement: In the tenth year of the mission, soon after the boycott ended, Abu Talib and Khadijah both died.
Abu Talib raised him from the age of eight and protected him through the years of the mission.

At Abu Talib's deathbed, with Abu Jahl and Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah present, he asked him to say 'la ilaha illa Allah'; they urged him not to leave the religion of Abd al-Muttalib; his last words were that he was on that religion; the Prophet said he would keep asking forgiveness until forbidden.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked against both narrations.

Paraphrase of meaning; the verse continues 'after it has become clear to them that they are companions of the Fire', omitted from the narration. Reviewer to decide whether the abridgement is acceptable.

statement: Qur'an 28:56 was revealed about Abu Talib.
Khadijah died three years before the Hijrah.
Her death was close to Abu Talib's, in the same year; the order and interval are disputed.
alternatives: Reports give the gap as three days, about a month, or two months; most place Abu Talib first.

statement: She had been his wife for twenty-five years.
notes: Follows from marriage at his age of 25 and her death in the tenth year.

statement: She covered him after Hira and said Allah would never disgrace him.
He said of Khadijah: I was given the gift of love for her.
notes: Direct speech. Content found in the Muslim dataset ('Her love had been nurtured in my heart by Allah Himself'); Arabic 'inni qad ruziqtu hubbaha'. Abd al-Baqi number from memory.

statement: The name 'Year of Sorrow' comes from later writers and is not established from the Prophet.
After Abu Talib's death Quraysh harmed him more; a man threw dust on his head; his daughter washed it weeping and he told her Allah would protect her father.
notes: From Ibn Ishaq; narrated with attribution.
